simple.meaning: לֶקֶט (leqeṭ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “the gleaning.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Leviticus, beginning at Leviticus 19:9. The surrounding contexts include land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לֶקֶט (H3951) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: לֶקֶט (leqeṭ) / H3951 is traced through Leviticus 19:9, Leviticus 23:22 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H3951. leqet לֶ֫קֶט noun [masculine] gleaning , i.e. what is or may be gleaned, only construct ׳ל קְצִירְךָ , as accusative of congnate meaning with verb לקט Pi`el, (q. v.) Lev 19:9 = 23:22 (H).

occurrences.englishText: “ ‘When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not wholly reap the corners of your field, neither shall you gather the gleanings of your harvest.

“ ‘When you reap the harvest of your land, you must not wholly reap into the corners of your field, and you must not gather the gleanings of your harvest. You must leave them for the poor, and for the foreigner. I am Yahweh your God.’ ”
